name: Direct Proportion and Unit Scaling
description: Scale cost, weight, quantity, distance, and output when both quantities move in the same direction.
script_scope: Teach direct proportion as a constant unit rate: if one quantity is multiplied by a factor, the dependent quantity is multiplied by the same factor. Build from cost per item and weight per length to dozens, mixed units, partial-work scaling, bundled quantities, and multi-factor cases where every factor is direct. Emphasize finding a clean scale factor before multiplying and checking that the answer moves in the expected direction. Prepare learners for the chapter's basic cost, weight, production, recipe and same-rate objective patterns without copying source questions.

name: Inverse Proportion and Fixed-Work Thinking
description: Recognize situations where increasing one quantity forces the target quantity to decrease.
script_scope: Teach inverse proportion through a fixed total: for the same work, workers × time stays constant; for the same distance, speed × time stays constant; for meshed gears, teeth × revolutions stays constant; for a fixed rope around cylinders, circumference × turns stays constant. Include missing-workforce problems and reverse reasoning. Make the learner ask what is being held fixed before deciding 'more means less', and guard against treating inverse situations as direct ones.

name: Compound Chain Rule: Direct or Inverse?
description: Handle several changing quantities by deciding how each one affects the target.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's chain-rule remark explicitly: compare every changing item with the quantity being found. Build a direction table mentally: if increasing a factor would increase the target, use it directly; if it would decrease the target, use it inversely. Cover two-factor and three-factor cases, earnings, output, lamps/cost, and symbolic proportional reasoning. The learner should be able to predict whether the answer rises or falls before calculating and use that prediction as a check.

name: Workers, Hours, Days, and Amount of Work
description: Use worker-hours-days as one work budget for standard labour and output problems.
script_scope: Teach the work-budget model for equal-efficiency workers: work is proportional to workers × hours per day × days. Cover finding days, workers, hours per day, output quantity, changed amount of work, half-time/double-work patterns, and symbolic forms. Use cancellation-friendly mental arithmetic. Distinguish 'same work' from 'more work' so learners know when work amount must enter the chain.

name: Equivalent Workers and Unequal Efficiency
description: Convert men, women, boys, machines, or other worker types into one common efficiency unit before applying chain rule.
script_scope: Teach mixed-efficiency questions by converting every worker type to one common unit before using time or work ratios. Cover statements such as '5 men = 9 women', one worker doing twice another's work, men/women/boys together, earnings by mixed groups, and machine/engine types with different consumption or work rates. Include one case where an equivalence must be deduced from two completed-work statements. The central habit is 'convert first, chain second'.

name: Changing Workforce, Remaining Work, and Deadlines
description: Split a job into stages when people join, leave, or the work rate changes partway through.
script_scope: Teach stage-based chain rule for jobs whose workforce changes. Cover absentees causing delay, extra workers needed after a known fraction of work is completed, workers added to recover a deadline, a team finishing early because daily output rises, and two-stage problems where hours per day also change. Emphasize that the first stage has already consumed part of the work, so only the remaining work belongs in the second chain. Include forward checks against the promised deadline.

name: Provisions, Rations, and Consumption
description: Treat food, medicine, and other supplies as a fixed stock consumed by people × rate × days.
script_scope: Teach provision problems with the stock model: total stock is proportional to number of consumers × daily consumption per consumer × number of days. Cover men leaving, reinforcements arriving, ration per head changing, dosage changing while patient count changes, mixed-equivalent consumers such as men and children, and reverse questions asking the original group size or stock duration. Always subtract the days already consumed before changing the population.

name: Machines, Production, and Dimensional Work
description: Scale production and physical jobs using machine-hours, efficiency, and job dimensions.
script_scope: Apply chain rule to production and geometric work. Cover machines × time × output, machine efficiency, pumps and quantities moved, trenches or canals where work is proportional to length × breadth × depth, wall length, pages × lines × letters, and mixed cases combining workers, hours and physical job size. Teach learners to turn dimensions into a single work-size factor before comparing resources and time.

name: Scales, Shadows, Gears, and Special Applications
description: Translate unusual word problems into the same direct/inverse relationships used by chain rule.
script_scope: Build transfer across the chapter's nonstandard contexts: map scales, similar shadows, photo enlargement, recipes and unit conversions, meshed gears, rope turns around cylinders, proportional bundles, and compact algebraic/symbolic chain-rule questions. Focus on identifying the invariant or common rate hidden in the story. The final capstone should combine unit conversion with a direction decision rather than reward formula memorization.
